languages.name: Zig
languages.description: Zig systems programming reference focused on builds, project detection, process execution, explicit memory, and WynCommand M4 tooling.

categories.name: Core Language
categories.description: Values, control flow, and compile-time features.

entries.title: const and var
entries.summary: Declare immutable and mutable bindings.
entries.signature: const name = value; / var name = value;
entries.definition: Declare immutable and mutable bindings.
entries.mental_model: const prevents rebinding; var allows mutation.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: if expressions
entries.summary: Branch and optionally produce a value.
entries.definition: Branch and optionally produce a value.
entries.mental_model: Control flow can directly compute values.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: const label = if (ready) "go" else "stop";

entries.title: switch
entries.summary: Pattern-match tagged values or integer-like values exhaustively.
entries.definition: Pattern-match tagged values or integer-like values exhaustively.
entries.mental_model: An exhaustive branch table checked by the compiler.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: for loops
entries.summary: Iterate over arrays, slices, or ranges.
entries.definition: Iterate over arrays, slices, or ranges.
entries.mental_model: Iteration binds each element explicitly.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: defer
entries.summary: Schedule cleanup code to run when the current scope exits.
entries.definition: Schedule cleanup code to run when the current scope exits.
entries.mental_model: Register cleanup next to acquisition.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
var file = try std.fs.cwd().openFile("README.md", .{});
defer file.close();
examples.explanation: Guarantees the file closes on scope exit.

entries.title: errdefer
entries.summary: Run cleanup only when the scope exits with an error.
entries.definition: Run cleanup only when the scope exits with an error.
entries.mental_model: Rollback cleanup specialized for error paths.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
const buf = try allocator.alloc(u8, 1024);
errdefer allocator.free(buf);
examples.explanation: Frees the buffer if later work fails.

entries.title: comptime
entries.summary: Evaluate code or require values during compilation.
entries.definition: Evaluate code or require values during compilation.
entries.mental_model: The same language executes in a compile-time phase.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
fn square(comptime n: usize) usize { return n * n; }
const x = square(6);

categories.name: Types and Error Handling
categories.description: Optionals, errors, slices, structs, enums, and unions.

entries.title: Error unions
entries.summary: Represent either a success value or an error.
entries.definition: Represent either a success value or an error.
entries.mental_model: Success and failure share one explicit type.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: try
entries.summary: Propagate an error union failure from the current function.
entries.definition: Propagate an error union failure from the current function.
entries.mental_model: Concise early return for errors.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: const value = try parse(true);
examples.explanation: Unwraps success or returns the error.

entries.title: catch
entries.summary: Handle an error union with a fallback or error binding.
entries.definition: Handle an error union with a fallback or error binding.
entries.mental_model: Turn the error branch into a chosen recovery path.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: const value = parse(false) catch 0;

entries.title: Optionals
entries.summary: Represent maybe-present values with ?T.
entries.definition: Represent maybe-present values with ?T.
entries.mental_model: Presence/absence is encoded in the type.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: Slices
entries.summary: Represent runtime-length views over contiguous elements.
entries.definition: Represent runtime-length views over contiguous elements.
entries.mental_model: Pointer plus length with explicit mutability.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
const text: []const u8 = "Wyn";
std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{text});

entries.title: Structs
entries.summary: Define product types with named fields and methods.
entries.definition: Define product types with named fields and methods.
entries.mental_model: Named fields laid out under compiler-controlled rules.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: const Macro = struct { key: []const u8, language: []const u8 };

entries.title: Enums
entries.summary: Define a finite set of named values.
entries.definition: Define a finite set of named values.
entries.mental_model: Tagged values ideal for exhaustive switch.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: const Mode = enum { build, test, run };

entries.title: Allocators
entries.summary: Request and free dynamic memory through explicit allocator interfaces.
entries.definition: Request and free dynamic memory through explicit allocator interfaces.
entries.mental_model: Memory policy is passed in rather than hidden globally.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
const data = try allocator.alloc(u8, 128);
defer allocator.free(data);

entries.title: ArrayList
entries.summary: Grow a dynamic array using an allocator.
entries.definition: Grow a dynamic array using an allocator.
entries.mental_model: Resizable buffer with explicit allocator ownership.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Appends a byte to a dynamic list.

categories.name: Build System
categories.description: Zig build graph concepts central to WynCommand M4.

entries.title: build.zig
entries.summary: Define project build steps in Zig code.
entries.definition: Define project build steps in Zig code.
entries.mental_model: The build is a programmable dependency graph.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: Build steps
entries.summary: Create named commands that depend on other build graph nodes.
entries.definition: Create named commands that depend on other build graph nodes.
entries.mental_model: User-facing commands are graph nodes with dependencies.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
const run_step = b.step("run", "Run app");
run_step.dependOn(&run_cmd.step);
